audit.why: EVEN / 6/10 against 48.65% over 1441 games. Gnar owns levels 1-2 on range, it evens once Abscond is up, and Sylas takes it back from his first AP item onward.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows contradicted the page's own whys and the packet. whys[0] says you win the first trade outright (stored Skill), whys[2] explicitly calls level 3 an 'even window' (stored Gnar), whys[5] says the first-item window is 'his window now' (stored Gnar), whys[6] says 'this window is his' (stored Gnar).
audit.why: Spike order is Gnar level 2, even from 3 through 6, then Sylas at first item and two items as Kingslayer's healing overtakes chip damage. The packet chart says exactly that.
audit.corrected: win[0]=Gnar, win[2]=Skill, win[5]=Sylas, win[6]=Sylas with matching phases sides, plus phases[2], [5] and [6] whys rewritten to fit their new owner. One atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors repeated across many fields. (a) Abduct (E2) is described as a stun in whys[2], spikes[1], early, mid, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and wants.foe[1]. Riot's description says he 'can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits' — it is a gap-close onto you, and the kit carries no hardCC flag on E at all. (b) Chain Lash is called his 'melee Q' twice; it is 775 range and actually out-ranges Mini Gnar's autos.
audit.why: Both change the trade. A player expecting to be stunned by Abduct will burn Flash or Hop pre-emptively and refuse trades he could win; a player told the Q is melee will step up to auto-range and eat it for free. The real danger in the combo is the Q-W follow-up healing him back through the chip, not the gap-close.
audit.corrected: Chain Lash (Q, 775 range, 10s at rank 1) lashes then detonates after a delay at the intersection — step off the mark and only the first hit lands. Abscond (E, 13s at rank 1) dashes; the Abduct recast pulls Sylas to you. Kingslayer (W, 12s at rank 1) heals off champions, which is what Grievous Wounds is for. Hijack (R, 80s at rank 1) takes GNAR!, so a sloppy transform hands him your own wall-stun.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Sylas must walk into your range.
edits.after: Abscond (E, 13s) lets him close and trade back, so level 3 is even — kite the recast, then punish the cooldown.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Abscond / Abduct's cooldown.
edits.after: His first AP item lets Kingslayer out-heal your chip — buy Grievous Wounds before you contest.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Sylas carry threat 8.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items in, full-AP Sylas out-sustains and deletes Mini — stop dueling in side lane and fight front-to-back.

edits.before: Mini Gnar's ranged autos plus a Boomerang win the first trade outright — his melee Q (Chain Lash) can't reach you and his Kingslayer heal is too weak early to undo it.
edits.after: Boomerang's 1100 range wins the first trade — Chain Lash reaches 775, so it out-ranges your autos but never the Q, and his heal is too weak to undo it.

edits.before: You stay favored kiting with Q slow and Hyper move speed, but his E1 dash into E2 Abduct stun lets him close and trade back — even window.
edits.after: You kite with Boomerang's slow and Hyper move speed, but Abscond into the Abduct recast closes the gap on 13 seconds — an even window.

edits.before: If Rage lines up for a Mega Wallop you can stun him as he lands his E2 (Abduct) grab; if you're stuck in Mini with Rage down, his E1 dash into E2 stun chains into Q-W and bursts your squishy ranged body.
edits.after: If Rage lines up, Mega Wallop stuns him as he lands the E2 (Abduct) pull; stuck in Mini with Rage down, Abscond into Abduct chains Q-W and bursts you — note Abduct drags him to you, it does not stun.

edits.before: Mini Gnar owns the first levels here — your ranged autos plus Boomerang out-range his melee Q (Chain Lash), and at level 2 you can land a free chunk and shove before his Kingslayer (W) heal is strong enough to matter. Don't dive in to extend a trade once he has E: he dashes with E1 (Abscond) and the second cast, E2 (Abduct), pulls and stuns you, letting him chain into Q-W and heal everything back. Poke, catch the Boomerang on its return for the cooldown refund, and keep your distance — he has almost no answer to ranged harass at level 1-3.
edits.after: Mini Gnar owns the first levels here — Boomerang's 1100 range beats Chain Lash (Q, 775), though that Q still out-ranges your autos, so poke with the throw rather than the walk-up. At level 2 you land a free chunk and shove before Kingslayer (W) heals enough to matter. Once he has E, don't extend: Abscond dashes in and the Abduct recast drags him onto you — a gap-close, not a stun — chaining Q-W to heal it all back. Catch the Boomerang on its return for the cooldown refund and hold your distance.

edits.before: This is the volatile stretch and it's pure Rage RNG. If Mega is up you can Crunch in and Wallop-stun him clean as he commits his E2 (Abduct) grab, or wall-ult him for a kill. If you're stuck in Mini with Rage on cooldown when he lands E, his stun into Q-W drain shreds your squishy body and heals him back up. At 6 he gets nothing new but neither do you — if you transform sloppily he ults, steals GNAR! and the wall-stun, and turns your signature combo against you. Only commit Mega when you can land Wallop before he can react.
edits.after: This is the volatile stretch and it is pure Rage RNG. With Mega up you Crunch in and Wallop-stun him clean as he commits the E2 (Abduct) pull, or wall-ult him for a kill. Stuck in Mini with Rage on cooldown when he lands E, the Q-W follow-up shreds your squishy body and heals him back up — Abduct itself only closes the gap. At 6 he gets nothing new but neither do you: transform sloppily and Hijack steals GNAR! and the wall-stun. Only commit Mega when you can land Wallop first.

edits.before: His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Abscond is 13s at rank 1; the Abduct recast pulls him onto you, it does not stun you.

notes: Main correction: Abduct was written as a stun in seven places. Riot's text describes it as a chain-pull that moves Sylas to the target, and the kit gives E only projectile and dash flags — no hardCC. I fixed the fields that actually teach the trade (whys[2], spikes[1], early, mid, dosFull[0]); breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and wants.foe[1] still carry the word 'stun' and need the same pass — they are near-duplicates of the focus string, so they will read cleanly once the focus template is re-themed. Second correction: Chain Lash is 775 range, not melee, and out-ranges Mini Gnar's autos.
